title: Brahma Sutra
attributionNote: Brahma Sutra, as Heritage IITKanpur's Scripture Server catalogues it (BRS), on its own shelf.
description: The Brahma Sūtra of Bādarāyaṇa, whom tradition identifies with Vyāsa, sets out the teaching of the Upaniṣads in four chapters of terse Sanskrit aphorisms, between 545 and 564 of them as the commentators divide them. Its subject is Brahman: the first chapter shows that the Upaniṣads speak of it with one voice, the second answers objections, the third sets out the means and the fourth the fruit, liberation. It is the reasoned member of Vedānta's three foundations, beside the Upaniṣads and the Bhagavad Gītā, and every school of Vedānta, Śaṅkara's, Rāmānuja's and Madhva's among them, wrote its own commentary on it. Its reader is the one who, having studied, asks what Brahman is: athāto brahma-jijñāsā. The summary above is the one Heritage IITKanpur's Scripture Server publishes for the text, and the server's own metadata records it as AI-assisted (claude-opus-5-5); an editor's note for the work itself is still to be written.
historicalContext: Read in the Heritage Scripture Server corpus, which continues the Gita Supersite built at IIT Kanpur: the text, its classical commentaries and the translations the server may serve are held together there.
availabilityNote: The outline is held: 16 chapter(s) and 577 verse address(es), read from the server's own catalogue. The verses are not stored — the licence forbids bulk harvesting and database reconstruction — and are streamed from the API one verse at a time as the work is read, with the attribution HCAL-1.1 requires and the server's own quota and licence notice.
